Definition: from G1909 and G839; occurring on the succeeding day, i.e. (G2250 being implied) to-morrow:--day following, morrow, next day (after).
BiblicalUsage: Epaurion simply means the next day, the morrow — and the Gospels and Acts are full of it. The next day John sees Jesus coming and says, Behold the Lamb of God; the next day Peter goes with Cornelius's men; the next day the disciples break bread at Troas. Ordinary days, carrying extraordinary things.
TheologicalSignificance: God works on plain tomorrows, not only on feast days, and the next day is often when the promise arrives. I hold that the Gospels' habit of saying 'the next day' is itself a sermon: keep walking, because tomorrow may be the day you meet the Lamb of God.
RelatedPeople: John the Baptist; Simon Peter; Paul
